newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BCN open to study partnerships.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BCN open to study partnerships.

text.p: Brazilian private bank BCN said it is not in merger talks with any financial institution, but noted it is open to partnerships if an attractive opportunity arose.
"We are not studying any proposal from any bank at the moment," BCN President Pedro Conde told reporters.
"But if, in the future, opportunities come up, we will analyse them," he added.
The market has speculated that the bank was holding merger talks with foreign banks, including Spain's Bilbao Vizcaya.
Earlier today, BCN announced it formed an equally-owned joint venture with U.S.-based Alliance Capital Management to provide asset management services in Brazil and, in a second stage, in Argentina.
Bilbao Vizcaya owns three percent of Alliance's capital.
Conde recognized that the bank has to adapt itself to Brazil's new banking environment.
"We have to study proposals to adapt ourselves to a globalized economy. Foreign banks are invading our market. We have to adapt ourselves to a new reality," he said.
"But the future is the future," he added.
Early this year, BCN decided to end negotiations with local bank Banco BBA Creditanstalt, which was interested in acquiring a controlling stake in the bank.

BCN then decided to invest in a new growth strategy, dividing the bank in three segments -- individual and corporate clients with annual revenues up to $5 million; companies with revenues between $5 million and $100 million; and firms with over $100 million in revenues.
It also decided to invest heavily in retail banking under a plan which includes the opening of branches in Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais states. The bank has now 203 branches.

BCN is Brazil's sixth largest private bank, with 14.06 billion reais in total assets and a 1.059 billion reais net worth, according to its first quarter results. It posted a net profit of 140 million reais in 1996.
